description: Polyphonic oscillator with one selectable waveform, carrying shape, phase, offset and level controls each with its own CV input and attenuverter

params.text: Picks the overall mode: audio, low frequency, 0Hz carrier for linear FM, or a triggered, retriggered or gated one shot that fires from the HARD SYNC input
Sets the oversampling applied to the audio output, off or x2 through x32; audio and 0Hz carrier modes start at x4 and the LFO modes start off
Switches on a high pass filter that removes DC offset from the output, off by default
Sets the base frequency, 16.352Hz to 4186Hz in audio mode with C4 at the centre and 0.125Hz to 32Hz in low frequency mode; in 0Hz carrier mode it is a bias of -0.08Hz to 0.08Hz
Selects the waveform: sine, triangle, square or saw
Shifts the frequency by as much as four octaves either way; in 0Hz carrier mode it sets the range of the linear FM depth instead
Momentarily forces the output monophonic so the channel count is recomputed, which restores the right polyphony in a patch with feedback
Sets the depth of exponential frequency modulation, -100% to 100%, and has no effect in 0Hz carrier mode
Sets the depth of through-zero linear frequency modulation, -100% to 100%
Picks the type of shaping the shape knob applies, from log/exp, J-curve, S-curve, rectify, normalized rectify, morphing and pulse width; the choices follow the waveform set by WAVE
Sets how much shaping is applied to the waveform, -100% to 100%, with the type of shaping set by the SHAPE mode button
Attenuates or inverts the CV for that control, and the result is summed with the knob value
Shifts the phase of the waveform as much as 180 degrees either way; driven at audio rates it gives phase modulation
Adds as much as 5V either way to the output, applied before the level
Sets the output level, -100% to 100%, at 100% by default

inputs.text: CV for exponential frequency modulation, ignored in 0Hz carrier mode; the port menu can turn its oversampling off
CV for linear frequency modulation, AC coupled and through-zero by default, with port menu options for DC coupling and for switching through-zero off
Attenuates the exponential FM depth, 10V for full depth and -10V for full depth inverted
Attenuates the linear FM depth, 10V for full depth and -10V for full depth inverted
Pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob; in 0Hz carrier mode it moves the bias at 0.02Hz per volt
A rising edge resets the oscillator phase to 0, and starts a cycle in the one shot modes; the trigger goes high above 2V and low below 0.2V
A rising edge reverses the direction of the waveform; the trigger goes high above 2V and low below 0.2V
CV for the shaping amount, summed with the shape knob after its attenuverter; 10V peak to peak covers the whole range
CV for the phase shift, summed with the phase knob after its attenuverter
CV for the offset, summed with the offset knob after its attenuverter
CV into the level through a VCA; port menu options make 5V equal 100% and make the VCA bipolar for ring modulation

outputs.text: The selected waveform, after its shaping, phase, offset and level

menu: Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
Disable DPW anti-alias — switches the alias suppression off in all audio modes, which gives smoother results for phase distortion work in 0Hz carrier mode
Limit level to 100% — on by default; switch it off and the level knob plus its CV is no longer clipped at 100%
LFO frequency as BPM — reads and displays the frequency knob in beats per minute rather than hertz while the module is in low frequency mode
Sync trigger threshold — High 2V, Low 0.2V by default, or High 0V, Low -2V, setting where the sync and reverse inputs count a rising edge
Audio mode default oversample — Off, x2, x4, x8, x16 or x32, the setting the OVER control takes on when the mode is changed to audio or 0Hz carrier; x4 by default
Disable oversampling, in a CV input's own port menu — leaves that one input unoversampled, which saves CPU on slow modulation
DC coupled, in the linear FM CV input's own port menu — stops that input being AC coupled, so a steady offset shifts the frequency
Disable through-zero, in the linear FM CV input's own port menu — stops the linear FM carrying the oscillator through zero into reverse
VCA unity = 5V, in the level CV input's own port menu — makes 5V rather than 10V stand for 100% at that VCA
Bipolar VCA (ring mod), in the level CV input's own port menu — passes negative control voltage and inverts the wave, which gives ring modulation
